title: 3rd Truth 1st Mystery No Degrees In Essential Power

questions.question: What is the main point of the First Mystery?
questions.answer: Allah’s power belongs essentially to His Being, so weakness can never touch it, and nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage say weakness cannot enter Divine power?
questions.answer: Because weakness is the opposite of power, and opposites cannot exist together in the same essential reality.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do different levels within a thing usually appear?
questions.answer: They appear when the opposite quality mixes in or resists it.

questions.question: What examples are given to show how degrees arise through opposites?
questions.answer: Light becomes stronger or weaker through darkness, heat rises or falls through cold, and strength varies through resistance.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the claim that Divine power has no degrees?
questions.answer: Allah creates all things with equal ease, as though each were only one thing.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about obstacles in relation to Divine power?
questions.answer: No barrier can block it, and no act of creation can burden it.

questions.question: How does the passage compare resurrection, spring, a tree, and a flower?
questions.answer: It says all of them are equally easy for Allah to create.

questions.question: Besides ease, what does the passage say about the quality of these creations?
questions.answer: Each is made with full art, wonder, and completeness, whether small or great.

questions.question: What would happen, according to the passage, if Divine unity were denied?
questions.answer: Even simple things would become extremely difficult to make, and creation would lose beauty and value.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the making of a flower, a tree, and a spring when Divine unity is not accepted?
questions.answer: A flower would become as hard as a tree, and a tree as hard as or harder than a spring.

questions.question: What effect would that false view have on living beings that now come into existence quickly?
questions.answer: They would take far longer to appear, or might never appear at all.

questions.question: Why do valuable and finely made fruits, flowers, trees, and animals appear so abundantly and regularly?
questions.answer: Because of the mystery that Allah’s undivided power creates them swiftly, easily, and without difficulty.

questions.question: What do these created things do after coming onto the scene of existence?
questions.answer: They carry out their roles, glorify Allah, and then leave behind seeds to continue their line.

questions.question: What larger belief does the First Mystery support?
questions.answer: It supports belief in Allah’s absolute power and oneness.

questions.question: In the First Mystery, what relationship is described between Allah’s Essence and His power?
questions.answer: The passage presents power as inseparably bound to His Essence.

questions.question: What logical principle is used to argue that Divine power cannot include weakness?
questions.answer: The principle that two opposites cannot be united in the same essential reality.

questions.question: Why are darkness, cold, and resistance mentioned?
questions.answer: They illustrate that differences in intensity come from the presence of opposing factors.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says there are no degrees in Divine power?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is not stronger in one case and weaker in another.

questions.question: How does the absence of degrees affect the act of creation?
questions.answer: It means creating many things or great things is no harder than creating one small thing.

questions.question: What does the passage say about weakness or deficiency in relation to Divine power?
questions.answer: Neither weakness nor lack can exist in it at all.

questions.question: How is the phrase about Allah being powerful over everything supported in the passage?
questions.answer: By explaining that resurrection, spring, a tree, and a flower are all equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What comparison shows that the passage is not only about quantity but also about artistry?
questions.answer: It says a flower is made with artistry matching a tree, a tree with wonder matching spring, and spring with fullness matching resurrection.

questions.question: What is the passage arguing against when it discusses what would happen without Divine unity?
questions.answer: It is arguing against the idea that creation can be explained without the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, how would denial of Divine unity affect artistic quality in creation?
questions.answer: Beauty and fine workmanship would disappear or lose their proper worth.

questions.question: What does the example of a living being made in a minute help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It shows how easy creation is under Divine unity and how impossible it would seem otherwise.

questions.question: What two qualities are repeatedly joined in the passage when describing created things?
questions.answer: Their great value and their widespread abundance.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the life cycle of fruits, flowers, trees, and animals?
questions.answer: They appear in order, fulfill their tasks, praise Allah, and leave seeds behind before departing.

questions.question: What kind of worldview is the passage trying to build in the reader?
questions.answer: A worldview in which all creation points to Allah’s perfect power, wisdom, and unity.

questions.question: What basic claim opens the First Mystery?
questions.answer: If a quality truly belongs to a thing’s essence, its opposite cannot enter that essence.

questions.question: How is that claim applied to Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Since power belongs essentially to Allah, helplessness can never be part of Him.

questions.question: What idea about opposites is treated as impossible in the passage?
questions.answer: The joining together of opposite qualities in one essential reality.

questions.question: Why does the passage discuss levels of light, heat, and strength?
questions.answer: To show that variation comes from opposing influences, not from the quality by itself.

questions.question: If Divine power has no opposing element mixed into it, what follows?
questions.answer: It has no levels, no weakness, and no limitation.

questions.question: What practical result follows from there being no levels in Divine power?
questions.answer: Nothing can stand against it, and no created thing is hard to bring into being.

questions.question: How does the passage use resurrection to make its point?
questions.answer: It presents the greatest restoration of life as just as easy for Allah as smaller acts of creation.

questions.question: Why are spring, a tree, and a flower grouped together in the argument?
questions.answer: They show a movement from larger to smaller examples, all of which are equally effortless for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say we can observe directly?
questions.answer: We can see these acts of creation taking place before our eyes.

questions.question: According to the passage, what mistaken result follows if Divine unity is removed from the picture?
questions.answer: Even simple natural things would become harder to explain than very large ones.

questions.question: In that mistaken view, what happens to speed in creation?
questions.answer: Quick creation would no longer make sense, and production would become extremely delayed or impossible.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the value and beauty of creatures in relation to their abundance?
questions.answer: They remain precious and finely made even though they are found everywhere in great numbers.

questions.question: What spiritual action do these creatures perform while carrying out their roles?
questions.answer: They declare Allah’s glory.

questions.question: What remains after they pass away?
questions.answer: Their seeds remain in their place.

questions.question: What is the central teaching of the First Mystery about Allah’s power and creation?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is perfect, without weakness or degrees, so every act of creation is easy for Him.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying a quality is essential?
questions.answer: It means the quality belongs inseparably to the very reality of the thing.

questions.question: Why would allowing weakness into Divine power be absurd in the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: Because it would mean combining power and powerlessness in the same essential reality.

questions.question: What pattern do the examples of light, heat, and strength share?
questions.answer: Each one changes only when an opposite factor enters and affects it.

questions.question: What does the passage infer from that pattern about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Since no opposite can enter it, it cannot vary or diminish.

questions.question: How does this argument answer the question of whether some creations are harder than others for Allah?
questions.answer: It says there is no difference in difficulty for Him between the greatest and the smallest.

questions.question: Which examples are used to illustrate equal ease in creation?
questions.answer: Resurrection, springtime, a tree, and a flower.

questions.question: What does the passage add about the excellence of these creations, not just their ease?
questions.answer: Each is made with fitting beauty, skill, and wonder according to its level.

questions.question: What claim does the passage make about the consequences of rejecting Divine unity?
questions.answer: Rejecting it would make creation irrationally difficult and strip it of its evident order and artistry.

questions.question: How does the passage overturn the assumption that small things are easier to explain without Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: It says even a flower would become as hard as a tree, and greater things even more impossible.

questions.question: What does the image of a creature now produced in a minute emphasize?
questions.answer: It emphasizes the speed and ease of actual creation under Divine power.

questions.question: How are abundance and preciousness related in the final paragraph?
questions.answer: The passage says created things can be plentiful while still being highly valuable.

questions.question: What is meant by creatures appearing on the plain of being?
questions.answer: They come into existence in an ordered and visible way.

questions.question: What final responsibility do the creatures leave behind when they depart?
questions.answer: They leave seeds that continue their line and witness to the same order.

questions.question: What truth about opposites forms the basis of the First Mystery?
questions.answer: An opposite cannot enter what belongs essentially to a thing.

questions.question: How does the passage use that truth in speaking about Allah?
questions.answer: It argues that because power is essential to Allah, incapacity cannot touch Him.

questions.question: What causes stronger and weaker forms of ordinary qualities in the passage’s examples?
questions.answer: The presence of opposing influences such as darkness, cold, or resistance.

questions.question: Why is this discussion important for understanding Divine power?
questions.answer: It explains why Divine power cannot increase, decrease, or contain levels.

questions.question: What does the lack of levels in Divine power imply about the creation of different things?
questions.answer: The creation of all things is equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about obstacles and Divine power?
questions.answer: No obstacle can hinder it in any way.

questions.question: How is the idea of equal ease expressed through the examples in the passage?
questions.answer: The greatest event and the smallest living form are all equally within Allah’s effortless power.

questions.question: What does the comparison between a flower and a tree show?
questions.answer: Smallness does not make something more or less artistic before Allah’s power.

questions.question: What role does Divine unity play in the logic of the passage?
questions.answer: It is the key that makes the ease, order, and beauty of creation understandable.

questions.question: What would become difficult if Divine unity were denied?
questions.answer: Producing even ordinary living things would become as hard as producing far larger realities.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the timing of creation under the false alternative?
questions.answer: Things that now appear quickly would take a very long time or not come forth at all.

questions.question: What combination of qualities in fruits, flowers, trees, and animals does the passage emphasize?
questions.answer: They are numerous and common, yet still valuable and full of art.

questions.question: What do these creatures do while they exist?
questions.answer: They perform the tasks assigned to them and glorify Allah.

questions.question: What sign of continuity remains after they leave?
questions.answer: Their seeds remain behind.

questions.question: What question does the First Mystery mainly answer about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It answers why nothing is difficult for Allah.

questions.question: What is said about a thing whose quality is essential to it?
questions.answer: Its opposite cannot enter into its essence.

questions.question: What opposite of power is discussed in the passage?
questions.answer: Weakness or impotence.

questions.question: Why can that opposite never apply to Allah?
questions.answer: Because Divine power is inseparable from His Most Sacred Essence.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the existence of higher and lower degrees in created qualities?
questions.answer: Such degrees come from mixing with or being opposed by contrary qualities.

questions.question: What examples are used to make that idea easier to grasp?
questions.answer: Variations in light, heat, and physical strength.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn about Allah’s power from those examples?
questions.answer: It has no degrees and admits no weakness, shortage, or obstruction.

questions.question: How does the passage use examples from creation to show equal ease?
questions.answer: It says Allah creates the final resurrection as easily as spring, spring as easily as a tree, and a tree as easily as a flower.

questions.question: What further point is made about artistic excellence in those examples?
questions.answer: Each level of creation is brought forth with matching perfection and wonder.

questions.question: What argument does the passage make about a world without Divine unity?
questions.answer: Without Divine unity, even the simplest created things would become impossibly hard to account for.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would happen to a living being that is now made quickly if that false view were true?
questions.answer: It would take much longer to appear, or perhaps never appear.

questions.question: What mystery explains the regular appearance of living things in great numbers?
questions.answer: The mystery of Allah’s unrestricted power working through His unity.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the behavior of these creatures after they appear?
questions.answer: They come in order, fulfill their purposes, praise Allah, and then pass on.

questions.question: What do they leave as a continuing trace of their existence?
questions.answer: They leave seeds in their place.
